citations.title: Cloudback Integration – Linear
excerpts:
Cloudback automatically backs up your Linear workspace on a configurable schedule, capturing issues, projects, documents, cycles, comments, labels, templates, initiatives, embedded files, and more. Backups are stored as encrypted, password-protected archives in your own cloud storage or built-in Cloudback storage.
When you need to recover data, Cloudback can restore your workspace to a different Linear workspace, making it useful for disaster recovery and workspace migration.

How it works ⁠

Cloudback connects to your Linear workspace via OAuth and runs scheduled backups automatically, with the option to customize the schedule.

...

You choose where backups are stored: your own AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, Alibaba Cloud, Wasabi, OneDrive (Business or Personal), OpenStack Swift containers, or built-in Cloudback regional storages.

## Linear MCP server

⁠

Your AI models and agents can use our official MCP server to access your Linear data in a simple and secure way.
Connect to our MCP server natively as a new Claude Integration, or by using the mcp-remote module in Cursor, Windsurf, and other clients.
We’re following the authenticated remote MCP spec, so the server is centrally hosted and managed. It has tools available for finding, creating, and updating objects in Linear like issues, projects, and comments — with more functionality on the way.

...

If you have questions, feedback, or requests for new MCP tools, please let us know.
We want to thank our partners at Cloudflare and Anthropic for helping us get up and running. For anyone in the community looking to build their own MCP server, Cloudflare provides excellent guides and hosting options.

1. Notify Linear’s customer support that you want to enable the service.

7. Confirm the API key and email address by clicking the “Enable SendGrid” button.
8. Finish the process by clicking the “Confirm” button.

Create and link issues with Sentry and automate issue creation

Convert Sentry exceptions into Linear issues for Triage review

Overview⁠

Create Linear issues from Sentry exceptions, link exceptions to existing Linear issues, and automatically create issues from Sentry based on alerts.

How it works⁠

After enabling this integration, an option to create or link Linear issues will appear in the right sidebar when viewing a Sentry exception. Create a new Linear issue or search for existing issues to link them. Linked issues show up in the right sidebar in Sentry with key details and Linear issues include a link to the corresponding Sentry issue.
The integration also supports creating Linear issues automatically. Create a new Sentry alert or add a Linear action to an existing alert in Sentry under Alerts.

citations.title: Sentry Agent Integration – Linear
excerpts:
Overview ⁠

The Sentry Agent helps teams resolve issues faster by bringing Seer’s root cause analyses directly into Linear. When you mention the agent in a Linear issue, it runs diagnostics in Sentry and posts back insights so you can quickly understand and act on problems without switching tools.

How it works ⁠

The Sentry Agent integration connects Sentry’s debugging insights with Linear’s issue tracking so teams can investigate and resolve problems without leaving their workflow. Once configured through secure OAuth, the agent listens for activity from both Sentry and Linear via webhooks, handling events like issue detail requests or Seer issue fix operations.
When triggered, it can initiate Seer runs in Sentry, generating root cause analyses that are posted back into Linear issues alongside other context so developers can quickly understand what went wrong and how to fix it.
